question: There are major concerns about per and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS). Some Member States have taken the lead and initiated national measures to restrict some of their uses.

The Commission’s response to a previous question was that ‘such measures are more efficient if taken at EU level by the established restriction procedure supported by a solid assessment by the scientific committees of the European Chemicals Agency’. A dossier for an EU-wide restriction of PFAS was submitted by five national authorities in January 2023.

We are now waiting for the opinions of the European Chemicals Agency (ECHA). In accordance with Article 71 of the Regulation on theRegistration, Evaluation, Authorisation and Restriction of Chemicals (REACH), the Committee for Socio-economic Analysis (SEAC) has 12 months to adopt its opinion. However, according to ECHA, SEAC is not expected to adopt its final opinion until the end of 2026.

This will be almost two years after the legal deadline. In accordance with Article 73(1) of REACH, the Commission is obliged to prepare a draft restriction within three months of the receipt of the SEAC opinion. Action against PFAS is long overdue, both in substance and legally.
Can the Commission give a commitment to respect the three-month legal deadline after receipt of the SEAC opinion and thus to present a draft restriction by March 2027 at the latest?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (16.2.

2026) The Commission takes the concerns expressed in the question of the Honourable Members very seriously and is fully committed to address the pollution caused by per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) and will seek to advance as rapidly as possible on the initiative of the five national authorities to restrict PFAS to protect the health of EU citizens and the environment.
The Commission has already shared in its Chemical Industry Action Plan1 of 8 July 2025 certain basic orientations in the interests of clarity and predictability.

Due to the unprecedented size, scope and complexity of this restriction proposal, the European Chemicals Agency requires additional time beyond that originally foreseen in the legal provisions of the Regulation on the Registration, Evaluation, Authorisation and Restriction of Chemicals2 to complete its assessment and issue its final scientific opinion, expected by the end of 2026.

On this basis, the Commission will prepare a well-balanced Commission restriction proposal. The Commission is confident that the manufacture and use of PFAS in the EU will be subject to a robust, proportionate and science-based regulatory approach, in order to protect human health and the environment while safeguarding critical industrial applications and critical industries.

In addition, it should be noted that, as stipulated in the Chemical Industry Action Plan, the Commission is pursuing a comprehensive strategy to support the transition away from PFAS. This strategy combines regulation with other measures.

Moreover, one of the objectives of the ECHA Regulation as well as of current reflections about the Registration, Evaluation, Authorisation and Restriction of Chemicals (REACH) is to lift bottlenecks and accelerate procedures.
